violated_contract: A client-side exemption from a metered/paywall gate must be conditioned on the request actually being served by the exempt path, not merely on the user having selected that provider in Settings. `isPushToTalkUsageLimitBlocked` exempted every push-to-talk turn once the Local provider was selected, but PTT's own routing (`PTTRoutePolicy.decide`) sends every online turn to Omi's cloud realtime hub regardless of which chat provider is selected — only an offline turn (on-device dictation, no AI response) ever avoids the hub. The exemption was therefore keyed to a UI selection that does not determine which backend actually answers the turn, letting a free user keep making cloud-backed PTT turns after exhausting their quota just by selecting Local.
canonical_prevention: When a metered gate has multiple serving paths gated by provider selection, the exemption must consult the same routing/admission decision the request will actually take (e.g. `PTTRoutePolicy.decide`'s online/offline split) rather than the static per-provider selection flag alone. Prove it with a behavioral test that pins the gate's outcome across the routing dimension (online vs. offline), not just across provider selection.
